messages:
incident-bot: ALERT 2105554321 | p99 latency spike + 5xx surge on /v1/generate in us-west-2 after canary deploy :rotating_light:

maya (sre): acked — I'm on it. tagging @lee (oncall) and @owen for routing changes.

lee (oncall): saw it in the dashboard — p95 up 3x, p99 timeouts at ~1.2s -> 6s. error rate 5xx from 0.2% -> 4.8%. Rolling requests show many "upstream timeout" in gateway logs.

owen (platform): recent canary pushed a routing config tweak to multiplexers: `keepalive_idle_threshold=90s` -> `10s` and `conn_backoff=fast`. Could be dropping warmed connections, causing cold starts and kv cache misses.

maya (sre): good candidate. can we verify connection resets? Lee, tail the gateway logs for RST and keepalive close.

lee (oncall): tailing now — lots of `HTTP/1.1 504 upstream read timeout` and TCP `RST` entries aligned with high latency spikes. sample logs:```[2026-03-15T20:07:12Z] req_id=abc123 gateway=proxy-7 upstream=mv-host:x.x.x.x status=504 backend_err="read timeout"```.

ben (support): any customer-facing impact? Support reports spike in error reports from two enterprise customers in ap-southeast. Adding them to the incident tracker.

maya (sre): hypothesis: the new keepalive/config increases churn, causing KV cache cold misses and higher p99. Need quick mitigation: revert canary or roll traffic back to stable. Also consider temporary increasing upstream timeouts to avoid 504s while we assess.

owen (platform): I can roll back the routing change from the canary immediately. Will also open a short-lived circuit breaker policy to fail fast to stable pool instead of retrying through the new route.

lee (oncall): performing quick curl checks against canary vs stable:```curl -s -D - -o /dev/null https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H 'x-canary: true' -w '%{time_total}\n'```

lee (oncall): canary avg time_total = 5.9s, stable avg = 0.42s.

maya (sre): roll back canary now. Owen, trigger rollback and scale stable up + route 100% to stable. ops-bot, create rollback runbook entry.

ops-bot: IR action created: rollback/2105554321 | initiated by owen at 2105554700.

owen (platform): rollback started — draining canary nodes, reattaching traffic to stable. ETA ~2m for traffic switch.

lee (oncall): watching metrics. p95 dropping already, p99 trending down. error rate falling from 4.8% -> 1.1%.

maya (sre): good signs. keep an eye for any regression in throughput. I'll keep tracing on a few long traces.

ben (support): contacting the two affected customers with a heads-up note: "we observed elevated timeouts after a canary deploy; we've rolled back and services are recovering; follow-up postmortem coming." They acknowledged.

lee (oncall): rollback complete, traffic at stable=100% as of 2105554905. p99 ~0.48s, 5xx back to baseline ~0.25%.

maya (sre): marking incident contained. next steps: postmortem, root cause confirmation (likely connection keepalive threshold + conn_backoff change), run more canary tests with traffic shaping and increased telemetry on KV cache misses, revert config in next safe deploy if needed.

owen (platform): saved canary config diff and will add a safety gate to prevent aggressive keepalive reductions without KV cache warmup metrics.

ben (support): will queue a customer follow-up email and flag enterprise SLO checks.

maya (sre): oncall handoff to Owen for post-rollback monitoring for 2 hours. @lee please update incident tracker with timeline and key traces.

lee (oncall): done — added logs, sample traces, and curl outputs. tagging for postmortem: @maya @owen @ben.

incident-bot: Incident 2105554321 marked CONTAINED at 2105555000 by maya (sre). Postmortem P1 scheduled.

maya (sre): thanks team. we'll run a focused canary with added connection stability checks before reintroducing the routing change. :thumbsup:
